61	available list and exits — that's the source of truth for which
62	benches the current build registers.**
63	
64	Flags (also visible via `-h` / `--help`):
65	- `-d`, `--duration SECONDS` — target wall-clock seconds per bench
66	  (default `5.0`); the outer loop runs until this time is reached
67	  (inner auto-sizes). See chores `0.3.1-dev1` for the empirical
68	  study behind the default — longer (`-d 30`+) gives
69	  publication-grade stability. Mutually exclusive with `-D`.
70	- `-D`, `--total-duration SECONDS` — target total wall-clock seconds
71	  across all requested benches; budget is split equally per bench
72	  (e.g. `-D 30` with 6 benches → 5 s each). Mutually exclusive with
73	  `-d`.
74	- `-o`, `--outer N` — override outer loop count (forces count-based
75	  mode instead of time-based; inner still adapts).
76	- `-i`, `--inner N` — override inner loop count per histogram sample.
77	  `inner=1` measures single-call latency (each sample = one step).
78	  Higher inner measures back-to-back / burst rate (each sample = N
79	  steps averaged, hides per-call jitter and parking costs).
80	- `--pin CORES` — pin bench threads to logical CPUs. `CORES` is a
81	  comma-separated list with optional ranges: `0,1`, `0-5`, `0,3-5,7`.
82	  Treated as a **core pool** indexed positionally with wrap-around, so
83	  thread `i` gets `pool[i % pool.len()]`. Examples:
84	  - `--pin 0,1` pins a 2-thread bench to logical CPUs 0 and 1.
85	  - `--pin 0,0` co-locates two threads on the same CPU
86	    (oversubscription — measures contention).
87	  - `--pin 0-11` defines a 12-CPU pool for larger fanout benches;
88	    threads wrap over it.
89	
90	  On AMD Zen 2 (e.g. Ryzen 9 3900X, 12 physical × 2 SMT = 24 logical
91	  CPUs), logical IDs `N` and `N+12` are SMT siblings of the same
92	  physical core. `--pin 0,12` pairs siblings (max resource contention);
93	  `--pin 0,1` uses independent physical cores in the same CCX (best
94	  latency for channel benches — shared L3, no SMT contention). Check
95	  your topology with
96	  `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/topology/thread_siblings_list`.
97	
98	  Typical measured effect on `mpsc-2t` at `-d 10` (3900X, idle desktop):
99	  unpinned mean ≈ 7,044 ns / stdev ≈ 6,545 ns / p99.99 ≈ 74 µs;
100	  `--pin 0,1` → mean ≈ 5,636 ns / stdev ≈ 1,321 ns / p99.99 ≈ 17 µs.
101	  Tail tightens ~4×, stdev ~5×, mean drops ~20 %.
102	- `--no-pin-cal` — skip pinning the main thread for calibration.
103	  By default, calibration runs with main pinned to `pin[0]` (if
104	  `--pin` is set) or core 0, so framing/loop numbers come from a
105	  stable environment regardless of `--pin`. Pass this flag to
106	  reproduce pre-0.6.0 behavior (main pinned iff `--pin` is given)
107	  for A/B comparison. No effect when `--pin` is set.
108	- `-v`, `--verbose` — print internals to stderr (affinity mask at
109	  startup, calibration parameters, raw `min_low`/`min_high`,
110	  precise fit values, calibration wall time). Equivalent to
111	  `RUST_LOG=debug`. Default filter is `warn` — silent unless
112	  something is wrong. `RUST_LOG`, when set, wins over `-v` so
113	  per-module filtering still works.

118	  Use this to inspect the underlying tick counts directly, e.g.
119	  when comparing against the counter frequency.
120	
121	Each bench prints a band-based histogram in nanoseconds. Bands are

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

Two long zcr runs (`-d 600`, `-d 300`) panicked at
`hist.record().unwrap()` with `ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled`:
the desktop idle-suspended mid-run, the in-flight sample spanned
the sleep, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the histogram's
60 s high bound. Journal `PM: suspend exit` timestamps match both
panics to the second. Sub-bound gaps are worse — they record
silently (`zcr-with-1t` logged a 40.6 s "sample": a ~22 min
suspend divided by `inner=33`) and poison mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s the report prints a `WARNING`
  naming the bench and gap; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle on the
  3900X, which is why the sleep gap appeared in samples at all —
  detection therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]],[[6]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

Two long zcr runs (`-d 600`, `-d 300`) panicked at
`hist.record().unwrap()` with `ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled`:
the desktop idle-suspended mid-run, the in-flight sample spanned
the sleep, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the histogram's
60 s high bound. Journal `PM: suspend exit` timestamps match both
panics to the second. Sub-bound gaps are worse — they record
silently (`zcr-with-1t` logged a 40.6 s "sample": a ~22 min
suspend divided by `inner=33`) and poison mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s the report prints a `WARNING`
  naming the bench and gap; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle on the
  3900X, which is why the sleep gap appeared in samples at all —
  detection therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

content.text:
Yes, I agree — on two counts, one of which I should have caught myself:

1. **The zcr bookkeeping I folded in.** I backfilled the zcr section's `Commits:` line (`[[6]]` for `de5dc57e`) and added the missing `[40]` definition inside this harness-fix commit. The protocol does say backfill rides "one push later" — but it doesn't say it must ride *inside* an unrelated change. A separate tiny notes-only commit (`chore: backfill zcr commit refs + [40] def`) keeps the harness fix pure. I'll split those edits out.

2. **The chores narrative leans on zcr.** The bug is a harness bug — any bench running while the machine suspends hits it. My section text opens with "Two long zcr runs..." and cites `zcr-with-1t`, which frames it as a zcr problem. The discovery context deserves maybe one sentence; the failure mechanism should be described bench-agnostically (a sample spanning a suspend; `inner=1` overflows the bound, `inner>1` poisons silently under it).

To be clear on scope after the split, the plan becomes three commits, each self-contained:

- `chore:` zcr bookkeeping only — `Commits:` backfill `[[6]]`, dangling `[40]` definition.

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]],[[6]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

Two long zcr runs (`-d 600`, `-d 300`) panicked at
`hist.record().unwrap()` with `ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled`:
the desktop idle-suspended mid-run, the in-flight sample spanned
the sleep, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the histogram's
60 s high bound. Journal `PM: suspend exit` timestamps match both
panics to the second. Sub-bound gaps are worse — they record
silently (`zcr-with-1t` logged a 40.6 s "sample": a ~22 min
suspend divided by `inner=33`) and poison mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s the report prints a `WARNING`
  naming the bench and gap; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle on the
  3900X, which is why the sleep gap appeared in samples at all —
  detection therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

## Todo

A markdown list of task to do in the near feature

  `Overhead::framing_per_sample_ns` ≈ 11 ns in an `adjusted`
  column, mirroring `harness::print_report`)
- Convert `harness` / `Bench` to probe-based measurement. Will
  likely need inner-loop support on `Probe` (batch N calls per
  sample; report divides by N and accounts for per-sample
  framing) so very-small workloads can still amortize timer
  overhead the way `run_adaptive` does today.
- Rename app

- `ice-ps-2t-wait` — iceoryx2 pub/sub with blocking waits via
  `Listener`/`Notifier` events; completes the {transport} ×
  {wait policy} matrix cell that compares against `mpsc-2t`
- Switch ice benches to the loan-based zero-copy send path
  (`loan_uninit` + `send`) — the API a perf-sensitive user would
  use, and closer to iceoryx2's own benchmark method
- Payload-size sweep for the round-trip benches (8 B / 8 KiB /
  1 MiB) — makes iceoryx2's size-independent latency vs channel
  copy cost visible in our own tables
- `crossbeam-1t` / `crossbeam-2t` — `crossbeam-channel` directly
  (compare to mpsc-1t/2t which use crossbeam under the std API)

  inside a Tokio runtime (async overhead)
- `flume-1t` / `flume-2t` — `flume` MPMC channel
- Function-call baselines: direct call vs `Box<dyn Trait>` vs

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

Two long zcr runs (`-d 600`, `-d 300`) panicked at
`hist.record().unwrap()` with `ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled`:
the desktop idle-suspended mid-run, the in-flight sample spanned
the sleep, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the histogram's
60 s high bound. Journal `PM: suspend exit` timestamps match both
panics to the second. Sub-bound gaps are worse — they record
silently (`zcr-with-1t` logged a 40.6 s "sample": a ~22 min
suspend divided by `inner=33`) and poison mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s the report prints a `WARNING`
  naming the bench and gap; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle on the
  3900X, which is why the sleep gap appeared in samples at all —
  detection therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

content.text:
That config is empty apart from a migration marker — the machine is on Plasma 6 defaults, so there's no explicit timeout to read. The journal shows suspends landing 38–49 minutes after each resume, and the timer counts from your last keyboard/mouse input, not from when the bench starts. That leads to two answers:

**There is no reliably-shorter `-d`.** 300 and 600 didn't trigger it because of their own length — six benches back-to-back kept the process running 30–100 minutes of wall clock, long enough for the idle timer to fire mid-run. A single bench with a short `-d` finishes before the machine ever gets sleepy. To trigger it via genuine idle you'd need one bench still running when the timer fires, so something like `-d 3000` (50 min), hands off the keyboard, then wake the box when you return.

**But you don't need to wait for idle — suspend it manually.** `systemctl suspend` takes the identical s2idle path the idle timer takes, so it's the same real test in ~2 minutes:

```
iiac-perf zcr-spin-2t -d 60        # the bench that panicked before
# ~10s in, from another terminal (or Ctrl+Z is no good — separate terminal):
systemctl suspend
# leave it asleep > 60s, then wake it with a keypress
```

Expected on the new binary: the run survives (previously this panicked), the in-flight sample clamps, and the report is preceded by both flags —

```
WARNING zcr-spin-2t: ...: system suspended ~90.0s during the run; data invalid
WARNING zcr-spin-2t: ...: sample(s) clamped at the 60s histogram bound; data invalid
```

If you wake it in under 60 s you'd see only the suspend warning (gap too small to clamp at `inner=1`). A 1t bench under the same treatment shows only the suspend warning too, since the gap divides by `inner`≈33 — that's the silent-poisoning case the detector exists for.

Since a wake needs a physical keypress, you're the necessary human in the loop: want to run it yourself as above, or shall I start the bench and issue the `systemctl suspend` at the right moment — you just wake the box after a minute or so?

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s the report prints a `WARNING`
  naming the bench and gap; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

In the report the p99-max shows:
  p99-max       510 ns    10,368,319,487 ns    10,368,318,978 ns      3,033,409    4,137 ns    4,126 ns

That reads 3,033,409 loops that were between 510ns and 10s of course there was only one at 10s, what if we had a row that was p99.999-max, isn't the other data is actaully valid?

content.text:
Your read is right, and it exposes both a reporting-granularity gap and an overstatement in my warning text.

**The band really is hiding the story.** `p99-max` there holds 3,033,409 samples (1% of 301M). The genuine content of that band is the ordinary scheduler tail — 510 ns up through a few ms of preemptions — plus exactly one 10.4 s suspend artifact, and the single artifact dictates the band's `last`, dominates its `mean` (4,137 ns), and poisons the whole-histogram mean/stdev. Finer boundaries would isolate it: with `p99.9`, `p99.99`, `p99.999` rows, 301M samples put ~3,000 samples in `p99.999-max`, and the artifact sits alone at the top of that row while `p99-p99.9` and `p99.9-p99.99` show the real tail structure. That's valuable for a latency tool regardless of suspends — tail structure is the point of the exercise. The band framework makes it a small change (extend `boundary_pcts`/`boundary_names`; empty bands already skip printing). One detail: the trimmed `mean min-p99` currently means "all bands except the last," so I'd anchor the trim at the p99 boundary explicitly to keep that metric's definition stable when more tail bands exist.

**And yes — most of the data is valid.** A ~10 s suspend corrupts the one in-flight sample plus a handful around it (the ~2 s of freeze/thaw machinery), all landing in the extreme tail. Everything else — every band below the tail, the percentile boundaries themselves (one sample out of 301M can't move even p99.999), and the trimmed min-p99 stats — is untouched. What's actually invalid: `max`, the untrimmed mean/stdev, and the top band's contents. So my `data invalid` wording overclaims; something like `max/mean/stdev poisoned` states precisely what died. The flag should still print — you want to know the run spanned a suspend — but it shouldn't condemn the whole report.

Proposal, keeping changes unconflated:

- **Pending fix commit** (uncommitted): soften the warning wording to name what's poisoned rather than declaring all data invalid. That text was born in this commit, so refining it here isn't conflation.
- **New separate commit**: `feat:` finer tail bands (`p99.9`/`p99.99`/`p99.999`), with the trim anchored at p99. Slots in before the docs commit.

Want me to do both?

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons mean/stdev untraced.

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

Both of those are pre-existing layout bugs, incidentally — visible in your very first transcripts (`stdev 1,002,824 ns` sat 2 columns right back then too), so they belong in the report-focused commits, not the suspend fix:

- **stdev off by 2**: column widths are computed only from the band rows' rendered strings. The summary `stdev` (161,068) is wider than the widest band mean (1,731), and Rust's right-align pads to a *minimum* width — wider content just overflows, shifting that line right by the difference. Fix: include the summary strings (mean, stdev, trimmed mean/stdev, adjusted values) in the width computation.
- **`meanadjusted`**: same mechanism on the header row — the `adjusted` label (8 chars) is allotted `" ns" + gap + adj_w` = 7+`adj_w` columns, so when adjusted values are single-digit (`adj_w`=1) the label exactly fills the field and lands flush against `mean`. vc-x1 0.67.0

Dual-repo commit+push+finalize in one resumable command.

Collapses today's manual Commit-Push-Finalize Flow into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

Stages: preflight (fmt/clippy/test) → review (approve diff)
→ message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →
commit-app → commit-claude (skipped if clean) → bookmark-both
→ push-app → finalize-claude. Failures in commit-app /
commit-claude / bookmark-both roll both repos back via
`jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-app.
After push-app succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and
recovery is forward-only.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body
across resumes so only the first invocation needs them.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in both repos (positional form of `--bookmark`).
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in both repos (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version
          Print the `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as the first line, then continue. With
          no subcommand, prints the banner and exits.
          
          Replaces clap's auto-version (which would exit after printing): the
          banner now rides along with normal subcommand execution rather than
          gating it, so scripts can capture the version *and* the command's
          output in one invocation.

      --restart
          Clear any saved state file and start from stage 1

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --from <STAGE>
          Explicit stage to jump to (advanced / debug use)

          Possible values:
          - preflight:       Run fmt / clippy / test / install / retest
          - review:          Present diff for the first approval gate
          - message:         Compose / edit the commit message; present for
            second gate
          - commit-app:      Commit the app repo
          - commit-claude:   Commit the `.claude` session repo (skipped if
            empty)
          - bookmark-both:   Advance both bookmarks to `@-`
          - push-app:        `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`
          - finalize-claude: `vc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --squash --push <b>
            ...`

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --status
          Print where the saved state thinks we are and exit

      --recheck
          Re-run `preflight` even on resume (default: skip if last run
          succeeded)

Dual-repo commit+push+finalize in one resumable command.

Collapses today's manual Commit-Push-Finalize Flow into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

recovery is forward-only.

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons `max` and the untrimmed mean/stdev
untraced (percentile bands and trimmed stats survive: a few
inflated samples out of millions land in the extreme tail).

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

```
Two pre-existing print_report alignment bugs, both from format

    from mean when adjusted values are narrow
  - print summary lines from the pre-rendered strings
- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: 0.13.1 -> 0.13.2
- notes/chores/chores-04.md: open section (empty Commits:)

```

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons `max` and the untrimmed mean/stdev
untraced (percentile bands and trimmed stats survive: a few
inflated samples out of millions land in the extreme tail).

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

## fix: report column widths

Commits:

Two pre-existing alignment bugs in `print_report`, both from
format widths being minimums that wide content silently
overflows:

- Column widths were computed from the band rows only, so a
  summary value wider than any band mean — typically the
  untrimmed stdev after a tail outlier — overflowed its field
  and shifted its line right. Summary values (whole-histogram
  and trimmed mean/stdev) are now rendered before the width
  pass and included in it.
- The `adjusted` header (8 chars) spans mean's ` ns` + gap +
  adj_w = 7 + adj_w header columns, so single-digit adjusted
  values (adj_w = 1) left the label flush against `mean`
  (`meanadjusted`). adj_w now floors at 3, keeping ≥ 2 spaces
  of separation.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons `max` and the untrimmed mean/stdev
untraced (percentile bands and trimmed stats survive: a few
inflated samples out of millions land in the extreme tail).

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

## fix: report column widths

Commits:

Two pre-existing alignment bugs in `print_report`, both from
format widths being minimums that wide content silently
overflows:

- Column widths were computed from the band rows only, so a
  summary value wider than any band mean — typically the
  untrimmed stdev after a tail outlier — overflowed its field
  and shifted its line right. Summary values (whole-histogram
  and trimmed mean/stdev) are now rendered before the width
  pass and included in it.
- The `adjusted` header (8 chars) spans mean's ` ns` + gap +
  adj_w = 7 + adj_w header columns, so single-digit adjusted
  values (adj_w = 1) left the label flush against `mean`
  (`meanadjusted`), and even 3-digit values gave only 2 spaces.
  adj_w now floors at 5, keeping the full 4-space gap between
  the two headers that every other column pair gets.

`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons `max` and the untrimmed mean/stdev
untraced (percentile bands and trimmed stats survive: a few
inflated samples out of millions land in the extreme tail).

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

## fix: report column widths

Commits:

Two pre-existing alignment bugs in `print_report`, both from
format widths being minimums that wide content silently
overflows:

- Column widths were computed from the band rows only, so a
  summary value wider than any band mean — typically the
  untrimmed stdev after a tail outlier — overflowed its field
  and shifted its line right. Summary values (whole-histogram
  and trimmed mean/stdev) are now rendered before the width
  pass and included in it.
- The `adjusted` header (8 chars) spans mean's ` ns` + gap +
  adj_w = 7 + adj_w header columns, so single-digit adjusted
  values (adj_w = 1) left the label flush against `mean`
  (`meanadjusted`), and even 3-digit values gave only 2 spaces.
  adj_w now floors at 5, keeping the full 4-space gap between
  the two headers that every other column pair gets.
- Headers right-justified to the digit end of their column,
  3 characters left of where the column visually ends (` ns`).
  Each label now right-justifies to the last character of its
  column's unit; unitless `count` still aligns to its digits.

# Chores 04

Continuation of [chores-03](../chores-03.md). Records landed work;
conventions in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) and
[cycle-protocol.md](../cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

## feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)

Commits: [[1]],[[2]],[[3]],[[4]],[[5]]

`../zc-ring-x1` exposes three API tiers per endpoint — raw
`reserve_slot` (caller handles Full/Empty), `reserve_slot_with`
(injected wait-policy closure), and `reserve_slot_spin` (built-in
spin policy). Its docs claim the no-wait fast path does the same
loads at every tier; add six benches `zcr-{raw,with,spin}-{1t,2t}`
to verify the tiers perform basically the same.

### As-built ladder

- 0.13.0-0 `chore: adopt cycle protocol + open zcr cycle`
- 0.13.0-1 `feat: zcr-raw-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-2 `feat: zcr-with-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-3 `feat: zcr-spin-1t/2t ring benches`
- 0.13.0-4 `docs: zcr tier comparison results`
- 0.13.0 `feat: zcr bench family (raw/with/spin, 1t/2t)` —
  close-out

The cycle was planned as 0.12.0 but renumbered at `-0`: the
session started from a working copy based on 0.11.0, unaware
the aarch64 ticks cycle (0.12.0, pushed from another machine)
already held `main`. The `-0` commit was rebased onto it —
`jj new main` → `vc-x1 sync` (no-op, already fetched) →
`jj rebase -r <prep> -d main` → conflict resolution (Cargo
version line; union-merge of `.claude/settings.local.json`) —
and the cycle renumbered 0.12.0 → 0.13.0.

### Tier comparison (0.13.0-4)

Method: installed `iiac-perf 0.13.0-4`, Ryzen 9 3900X, idle
desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;
values are the adjusted trimmed mean (min-p99). Run 2 repeats
the 2t trio to check repeatability.

| bench        | run 1  | run 2  |
|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

Observations:

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.
- 2t: `with` and `spin` are identical (~100 ns) — expected,
  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.
- We think the raw 2t penalty is in the waiting path, not the
  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.
- Transport context: the zcr 2t rows (~100-120 ns) sit at or
  under `mpsc-2t-spin` (117 ns) and ~6x under `ice-ps-2t`
  (656 ns) at the same wait policy.

Net: the ergonomic tiers cost nothing over raw — and under
cross-core traffic the DIY retry loop is the *slowest* way to
wait.

## fix: saturate hist records, flag suspended runs

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the
histogram's 60 s high bound (journal `PM: suspend exit`
timestamps match both observed panics to the second). A
sub-bound gap is worse — divided down by `inner`, it records
silently and poisons `max` and the untrimmed mean/stdev
untraced (percentile bands and trimmed stats survive: a few
inflated samples out of millions land in the extreme tail).

- `saturating_record` replaces `record().unwrap()`: a sample
  above the bound clamps at 60 s instead of panicking the run;
  a clamp pileup stays visible in the `max` column.
- Suspend detection (`ClockPair`): capture `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` +
  `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` at run start; MONOTONIC freezes during
  suspend, BOOTTIME keeps counting, so their elapsed divergence
  is the suspended time. At ≥1 s a `WARNING` naming the bench
  and gap prints as the report's last line — after the table, so
  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second
  `WARNING` (covers a wedged sample with no suspend).
- The 60 s bound is a sane-world ceiling, not a type limit
  (u64 ns holds ~584 years); recording the "true" hours-long
  value would only distort mean/stdev further, so clamp + flag
  beats raising the bound.
- We think minstant's TSC keeps counting across s2idle, which
  is why the sleep gap appears in samples at all — detection
  therefore uses std `Instant`, not minstant.

## fix: report column alignment

Commits:

Pre-existing alignment problems in `print_report` — two bugs
from format widths being minimums that wide content silently
overflows, plus header justification that read poorly:

- Column widths were computed from the band rows only, so a
  summary value wider than any band mean — typically the
  untrimmed stdev after a tail outlier — overflowed its field
  and shifted its line right. Summary values (whole-histogram
  and trimmed mean/stdev) are now rendered before the width
  pass and included in it.
- The `adjusted` header (8 chars) spans mean's ` ns` + gap +
  adj_w = 7 + adj_w header columns, so single-digit adjusted
  values (adj_w = 1) left the label flush against `mean`
  (`meanadjusted`), and even 3-digit values gave only 2 spaces.
  adj_w now floors at 5, keeping the full 4-space gap between
  the two headers that every other column pair gets.
- Headers right-justified to the digit end of their column,
  3 characters left of where the column visually ends (` ns`).
  Each label now right-justifies to the last character of its
  column's unit; unitless `count` still aligns to its digits.

# References

[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/commit/8aaccf8518c4 "8aaccf8518c4cb46bcc2fbf96a317d5d4c962f68"
[2]: https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/commit/1043a8c53feb "1043a8c53feb0e9a10bafa0cff68eb23e13b181f"

[4]: https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/commit/7251ad8e8e65 "7251ad8e8e65ad7d67883f15f7c32d4650b45c48"
[5]: https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/commit/e7f138342c58 "e7f138342c58b73daf4545846644b0ecfcbc625a"

content.text:
Those are the genuine article — real OS and hardware noise on an unpinned desktop run, and they're exactly what this tool exists to characterize. Reading your band structure (my `-d 5` run, same shape as yours), each tier has a distinct signature:

- **`p99-p99.9`, ~150k samples at 495–665 ns**: too many to be OS events — that's one round-trip occasionally taking a few extra spin iterations. We think it's cache-coherence variance: the line carrying the ring index ping-pongs between cores, and occasionally a snoop/arbitration delay or SMT-sibling traffic makes the store propagate slower. Hardware-level jitter, not the kernel.
- **`p99.9-p99.99`, ~14k at 0.7–2.7 µs**: the right magnitude and rate for interrupt handling — timer ticks and device IRQs landing on the measuring or echoing core (~1.4k/s across two spinning threads is plausible tick+IRQ traffic).
- **`p99.99-p99.999`, ~1.5k at 2.7–11 µs**: softirq work and short involuntary preemptions.
- **`p99.999-max`, ~162 at 11–210 µs**: full deschedules — the scheduler gave the core to something else (desktop background work) for a timeslice. ~32/s across two unpinned threads on a busy desktop is unremarkable.

The magnitude attributions past the first band are inference from typical costs, not measured causality — but the structure supports it, and it's why the trimmed `min-p99` row exists: the mean answers "what does a round-trip cost," the tail bands answer "what does my machine do to me."

Two knobs you already have to test this: `--pin 0,1` (your own README data: p99.99 tightens ~4× when pinned — it removes migrations and some preemption), and a quieter machine. The remaining tail after pinning is mostly IRQs/SMIs, which need `isolcpus`/`nohz_full`/IRQ affinity to chase further — potential future todo if you want publication-grade tails.

content.text:
Yes on consistency, with one big caveat on "fastest": `--pin 0,12` on your 3900X is the **SMT-sibling pair** — logical CPUs 0 and 12 are the same physical core. That's why this run is so fast: the ring's cache lines live in the L1/L2 that both hyperthreads share, so a "cross-thread" hop never leaves the core. You're seeing 35 ns adjusted trimmed vs ~100 ns for two real cores (`--pin 0,1`, your earlier tier-comparison numbers). It's a legitimate configuration — some real systems do co-locate producer/consumer on siblings for exactly this reason — but it's measuring intra-core communication, not the cross-core case most deployments hit.

So for optimizing an algorithm:

- **Pinning buys you repeatability**, which is the thing that matters for A-vs-B: no migrations, stable cache topology, tight stdev (your `stdev min-p99` dropped to 3 ns — that's publication-grade consistency in the body of the distribution).
- **Which pinning to use depends on what you're optimizing for.** Hold it constant across variants and the *relative* comparison is valid at any tier. For *absolute* numbers, pick the topology matching deployment: `0,12` = shared-core best case; `0,1` = same-CCX cross-core through shared L3 (the usual realistic tier); on a 3900X you also have cross-CCX (`--pin 0,3`) and cross-CCD (`--pin 0,6`) tiers, each adding fabric latency. Running the same bench across those tiers is itself a useful experiment — it tells you how coherence-sensitive the algorithm is.
- Note the tail didn't disappear: 1,232 samples at 58–916 µs even pinned. Pinning constrains *your* threads, it doesn't reserve the core — the desktop still preempts you. The trimmed row dodges that; eliminating it needs core isolation.

One more thing your run shows: with the faster step (37 ns), the harness auto-sized `inner` to 3, so each sample now averages 3 round-trips — fine for the mean, but it dilutes single-call tail resolution; `-i 1` restores per-call sampling if you're studying the tail specifically.

aiTitle: Fix u64 overflow in iiac-perf benchmarks

content.text:
Good instinct with the power button — and your machine's state explains the asymmetry:

**Why the power button always works:** it isn't a peripheral. It's wired to the chipset as an ACPI *fixed event*, delivered over the ACPI SCI interrupt, and the spec requires it to be armed as a wake source in every sleep state — no driver, no USB stack, no configuration involved. Your `/sys/power/pm_wakeup_irq` reads `9`, the ACPI SCI, confirming the last wake came in exactly that way. A short press is just a wake event (it only becomes "power off" via a long ≥4 s press, which is a firmware hard-cut), so it was always the right thing to try before the reset button.

**Why the keyboard is unreliable:** a USB keystroke waking the box is the end of a long conditional chain — the keyboard must have remote-wakeup armed, every hub between it and the controller must be armed, the xHCI controller must arm PME before entering D3, and that PME must be routed to a wake-capable interrupt. Every link has to hold. On your box the links are actually *not* formally armed: all ten USB root hubs report `power/wakeup: disabled` (only the controller `XHC0` is enabled at the ACPI level). So keyboard wake on this machine was never guaranteed configuration-wise — we think the earlier suspends woke on keypress because the controller happened to still be in a responsive state when you pressed, and on the last cycle it had fully quiesced into D3 with no remote wake armed, leaving the keyboard electrically mute. AMD xHCI wake arming is also known to be flaky across repeated s2idle cycles, which fits your "several worked, then one didn't" pattern.

If you want keyboard wake to be dependable: `echo enabled | sudo tee /sys/bus/usb/devices/usbN/power/wakeup` for the hub chain your keyboard hangs off (made persistent with a udev rule). For bench purposes though, the power button is the robust wake path — and once the inhibit step lands, wake-from-suspend stops being part of the workflow at all.

That count is actually the design working, not a surprise in the data — `p99.999-max` holds the top 0.001% *by definition*, and 0.001% of 125.6M samples is ~1,256. desktop, `iiac-perf zcr mpsc-2t-spin ice-ps-2t -d 5 --pin 0,1`;

the 2t trio to check repeatability.

|--------------|-------:|-------:|
| zcr-raw-1t   |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-with-1t  |   4 ns |      — |
| zcr-spin-1t  |   5 ns |      — |
| zcr-raw-2t   | 119 ns | 120 ns |
| zcr-with-2t  | 101 ns | 101 ns |
| zcr-spin-2t  | 101 ns |  99 ns |
| mpsc-2t-spin | 117 ns |      — |
| ice-ps-2t    | 656 ns |      — |

- 1t: all three tiers are identical within noise (4-5 ns).
  The no-wait fast path costs the same at every tier, matching
  the zc-ring-x1 doc claim that `_with`'s fast path does
  exactly the loads `reserve_slot` does.

  `reserve_slot_spin` *is* `reserve_slot_with(policy::spin)`.
  `raw` is consistently ~20 ns slower (119-120 ns) across
  runs.

  fast path: the hand-written retry loop re-enters
  `reserve_slot` on every failed attempt — re-running the type
  check and re-loading the caller's own index each time — while
  `_with` hoists the own-index load out of the loop and re-reads
  only the peer index per attempt, so it reacts faster when the
  peer's index store lands.

Commits:

The harness panicked at `hist.record().unwrap()` with
`ValueOutOfRangeResizeDisabled` when the desktop idle-suspended
during long runs: a sample that spans a suspend measures the
whole sleep gap, and at `inner=1` the raw gap exceeded the

  it can't scroll out of mind; a clamped `max` prints a second

  summary value wider than any band mean — typically the
  untrimmed stdev after a tail outlier — overflowed its field
  and shifted its line right. Summary values (whole-histogram
  and trimmed mean/stdev) are now rendered before the width
  pass and included in it.

  adj_w = 7 + adj_w header columns, so single-digit adjusted
  values (adj_w = 1) left the label flush against `mean`
  (`meanadjusted`), and even 3-digit values gave only 2 spaces.
  adj_w now floors at 5, keeping the full 4-space gap between
  the two headers that every other column pair gets.

  3 characters left of where the column visually ends (` ns`).
  Each label now right-justifies to the last character of its
  column's unit; unitless `count` still aligns to its digits.

isolate in `p99.999-max` while the lower tail bands show the
genuine scheduler-preemption structure.

  (label `min-p99` unchanged): the trim excludes every band at
  or above p99, independent of how many finer bands subdivide
  the tail.
- Empty bands were already skipped in the output, so runs with
  few samples print only the tail rows they can populate.
